findings.reason: The protected source is the conventional optimal in-place sign-marking solution. Its single pass, direct value-to-marker mapping, and descriptive duplicate accumulator are concise and immediately explainable in an interview; an inert candidate would not materially improve it.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 442 and its Python array-to-array surface. The app solve signature and native findDuplicates method both accept nums and return every value occurring twice. The modular Reference preserves the exact value range, once-or-twice frequency guarantee, arbitrary result order, required bounds, and all three source examples.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064825676. The app and native implementations have the same loop, absolute-value recovery, value-minus-one marker location, negative-marker duplicate test, append behavior, and first-visit negation; only type annotations and the required Solution wrapper differ.

The 64-, 192-, and 512-element benchmark tiers span 8x and exercise paired values while the protected source performs one constant-work visit per element. It passed all 10 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.02x the reference runtime. A correct O(n^2) repeated-count control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 1.55x.

The Approach exactly describes the protected source: recover the absolute current value, map it to position value - 1, negate a positive marker on first sight, and append after finding a negative marker. It also explains why the at-most-twice guarantee reports each duplicate once and accurately states O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

The hash-bound Reference was checked against the live public statement. It preserves the array domain and frequency conditions, requested duplicate values, linear-time and constant-auxiliary-space requirement, all three examples in source order without invented explanations, and all four constraints. The source contains no tables, diagrams, images, notes, or follow-up section.
